newsitem.title: USA: P&G purchaser is among U.S. crash victims - P&G.
newsitem.headline: P&G purchaser is among U.S. crash victims - P&G.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Co. said on Friday it lost an employee in Thursday's crash of a Comair commuter flight near Detroit.
In addition, a young woman was killed whom the consumer products manufacturer had just interviewed and offered a job, spokeswoman Linda Ulrey said.
Dexter Adams, 41, was a senior purchases manager, buying fragrances for cleaning products globally. He was en route to the University of Michigan to recruit potential employees, Ulrey said.
Arati Sharangpani, whose home Comair listed as Coldsneck, N.J., had just been offered a job, Ulrey said. Sharangpani was due to be graduated in June from the University of Michigan, Ulrey said.
"We, unfortunately, lost not only a valued employee, but a potentially fine future employee whom we felt was a nice, talented young lady," she said.
Adams, a Cincinnati resident, had been with P&G since 1987. A West Point graduate and U.S. Army veteran, he leaves a wife and two children.

Adams and Sharangpani were among 26 passengers and three crew members who died when the Comair flight 3272, bound from Cincinnati to Detroit, crashed in a rural area near Monroe, Mich., about 25 miles (40 km) southwest of Detroit.
Comair, Inc. is a Cincinnati-based regional airline that flies commuter routes for Delta Air Lines Inc.
